body.text: Overview and Empirical Foundations of Zram
Reliable software systems depend on foundational primitives like Zram. Understanding how it manages state, latency, and fault tolerance separates resilient architecture from fragile code.

a RAM disk with on-the-fly disk compression. The block device created with zram can then be used for swap or as a general-purpose RAM disk. The two most common uses for zram are for the storage of temporary files (/tmp) and as a swap device. Initially, zram had only the latter function, hence the original name "compcache" ("compressed cache").

14, released on March 30, 2014. 15 onwards (released on June 8, 2014), zram supports multiple compression streams and multiple compression algorithms. Compression algorithms include DEFLATE (DEFLATE), LZ4 (LZ4, and LZ4HC "high compression"), LZO (LZO-RLE "run-length encoding"), Zstandard (ZSTD), 842 (842). 1, the default is LZO-RLE, which has a balance of speed and compression ratio. Like most other system parameters, the compression algorithm can be selected via sysfs.
